title: Add independent harmonic-kind coverage and selective spelling-loss policy
scope: Complete pinned-consumer regression coverage for all retained harmonic kinds/fractional frets and isolate the existing legacy spelling omission contract.
acceptance: For Natural, Artificial, Pinch, Tapped, Semi, and Feedback separately at FretFloat=2.4, assert exact HType/HFret XML, Go kind and fractional fret, and pinned consumer kind and fret; no spelling-loss report without authored Pitch/Octave.

For natural and artificial harmonics, independently exercise non-default Pitch, Octave, and both together. Preserve the public source fields before export, emit exactly gp8.omit.harmonic-pitch for that authored pair, reject strict export until that code is allowed, and verify allowed output retains kind/fret while omitting only the unsupported spelling fields.

Keep spelling loss independent from Fret/FretFloat authority: a matching legacy integer view2 and exact2.4 does not itself need the spelling-loss code; a truly conflicting legacy fret gets its existing separate authority report and cannot be bypassed by allowing only harmonic-pitch.

Use explicit consumer expectations per kind and fractional fret; add the independent consumer evidence and precise allowed-loss assertions to the semantic ledger. Keep spelling/octave export partial and supported kind/fret slices unchanged.
exclusions: No mapping harmonic-specific spelling to generic note Tone/Octave or alteration of sounded pitch; no invented dedicated GPIF spelling record; no broad support promotion.

reproduction.instructions: Extend TestConformanceHarmonicVariants and authority controls. Existing 2.4 cases decode XML and reparse Go; load the same outputs with pinned oracle and compare effects.harmonic.kind/fret. Existing C# PitchClass and OctaveOttava values are valid source examples for isolated spelling reports. Add the selective allow-list matrix without duplicating existing rejection-only checks.

evidence.detail: Public contract; linked matrix cases are in obligation.

target-limit: Harmonic kind/fret are supported; legacy harmonic-specific pitch/octave spelling has no retaining target destination.
